newsitem.title: USA: Black & Decker sees Q4 profit below views.
newsitem.headline: Black & Decker sees Q4 profit below views.

text.p: Black & Decker Corp said its earnings were likely to be lower than the current consensus estimates of about $1.00 per share in the fourth quarter and $2.40 per share for the 1996 year.
In a statement, Nolan D. Archibald, chairman and chief executive officer, cited lower than anticipated sales in its Power Tools and Accessories business.
Archibald said that 1996 earnings were still expected to "substantially exceed comparable 1995 results."
The company also said it was "likely that 1997 first quarter earnings will be lower than for the same period of 1996." It did not elaborate.
The company said that it expected sales growth likely to be in the two-to-three percent range in the fourth quarter, rather than the five-to-six percent range previously seen.
It said fourth quarter earnings of $0.90 per share in 1995 included about $0.10 cents related to PRC Inc, a business which has been sold.
The company said its Power Tools and Accessories business was hurt by weak economies in Europe.

"Despite substantial cost reductions implemented there during 1996, we were unable to leverage an improved cost base with as much sales growth as we had hoped," it said. "We are beginning, however, to see some improvement in European markets, and our new products are doing well."

The company said it was "optimistic that the rate of sales growth will increase through 1997. We also expect to benefit next year from significant incremental cost savings associated with our ongoing European restructuring program."
It said that in Latin America, it suffered sales shortfalls due to the transfer of production to a new, lower cost facility in Brazil during the quarter.
It said that once issues in Brazil and at its new plant in Mexicali, Mexico, are resolved, overall production costs will be enhanced.
It said the sales pace in the Far East was hampered by a competitive business climate.
It added that because a revised North American sales outlook will affect its geographic mix of earnings, it anticipates a full-year tax rate lower than 27 percent reported for the first nine months.
It said that a favorable tax adjustment will be recorded in the fourth quarter. The adjustment will partially offset the impact of our reduced operating results.
